title: Junctional rhythms
categories: Sinus rhythm with a junctional escape beat

items.name: Sinus rhythm with PJCs
rows: Early beat: inverted P with a short PR
action: Usually benign
Treat the cause; check for digoxin toxicity
options: Sinus rhythm with a junctional escape beat
hints: Find the early beat. Is the QRS narrow, and what does its P wave look like?
Here's what I measure on this one: rate ≈ 70/min (6-second count); underlying 63/min; rhythm regular except the early beat; PR 0.19 s on sinus beats; QRS narrow (0.09 s).
The early beat is narrow, and its P wave is inverted or missing.

items.name: Junctional rhythm
action: Junctional escape at 40–60/min
Treat as bradycardia if symptomatic; review medications
options: Sinus rhythm with a junctional escape beat
hints: Look for P waves: are they upright, inverted, missing or after the QRS? Then count the rate.
Here's what I measure on this one: rate 59/min; rhythm regular; PR not measurable; QRS narrow (0.09 s).
Narrow and 40–60, with no normal upright P waves.

items.name: Accelerated junctional rhythm
action: Junction firing at 60–100/min
Consider digoxin toxicity or ischemia; monitor
hints: Check the P waves first, then compare the rate with the junction's usual 40–60.
Here's what I measure on this one: rate 63/min; rhythm regular; PR none (P follows the QRS); QRS narrow (0.07 s).
It's narrow and regular with no upright P, at a normal rate.

items.name: Junctional tachycardia
action: Junction firing over 100/min
Treat the cause (digoxin, ischemia, stimulants); tachycardia algorithm if unstable
options: Sinus rhythm with a junctional escape beat
hints: Look just in front of each QRS for the P wave's direction, then count the rate.
Here's what I measure on this one: rate 149/min; rhythm regular; PR none (P follows the QRS); QRS narrow (0.09 s).
Inverted P waves sit just before each QRS at a rate over 100.
